requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: app/Models/Entity.php:51 owner() (HasOne filtered to UserRole::Owner), app/Models/EntityMembership.php:33-53 local scopes, app/Models/User.php:38,46,56 memberships()/entities()/membershipFor(), app/Models/UserRole.php:17 manageable() = [Admin, Employee], both factories (database/factories/EntityMembershipFactory.php:30,35,40 states), and database/migrations/2026_10_29_043320_create_entity_memberships_table.php:21-26 implements owner_seq as a stored generated column with the exact named unique indexes. Policies implement each rule exactly (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:15-41; app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:12-38), including the owner-membership-never-deletable and self-removal cases. Docs/changelog updated (docs/database-schema.md:3,139,152-154).

conventions.evidence: Migrations use the generated Schema::create boilerplate and a reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_043319_create_entities_table.php:14,26-28). Mass assignment is deliberate via #[Fillable] matching the existing User model style (app/Models/Entity.php:14, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13). Authorization lives only in app/Policies/*, no controller/UI logic. Docs kept in sync (docs/database-schema.md intro + modeling notes) and CHANGELOG.md:12. Tests are Pest with RefreshDatabase.

security.evidence: All authorization is server-side in App\Policies\EntityPolicy and EntityMembershipPolicy (e.g. app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:26-38), with no reliance on UI. The generated owner_seq column is intentionally absent from $fillable (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13), so mass assignment cannot write it. #[$fillable] is narrowly scoped to name/slug and entity_id/user_id/role. No Blade/output/escaping surface exists in this change, and non-members are denied everywhere (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:20,43-46).

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:13-146 covers schema and index names, enum values, route key, factory defaults/uniqueness, soft deletes, scopes/relations, DB-level rejection of a second owner and duplicate memberships; tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php:21-99 exercises every policy path for owner/admin/employee/non-member plus cross-entity outsiders and the owner-delete/self-removal cases. Gap: only the user-delete cascade is asserted (tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:141); the entity_id cascade declared at database/migrations/2026_10_29_043320_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16 has no test.

simplicity.evidence: Lean implementation: reuses HasFactory, the project's #[Fillable] attribute style, attribute scopes, and User::membershipFor() rather than adding services/repositories; owner() is a single filtered HasOne (app/Models/Entity.php:51). No speculative abstraction or dead code. Only minor duplication is the identical private isManager() helper in both policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:48, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:35).

readability.evidence: Small, focused, typed methods with accurate PHPDoc generics (app/Models/Entity.php:27-52, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:31-69, app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:43-50); names state the domain rule (manageSettings, assignRole). Style matches sibling files, no debug output. Minor: the test file declares a global memberOf() helper (tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php:13).

scope.evidence: Diff is limited to the task: two migrations, three models/enum, two factories, two policies, two test files, plus the required docs/database-schema.md update and a CHANGELOG entry. No routes, Livewire, session, navbar, translations or unrelated refactors; the change.diff touches only these files.

issues.explanation: The cascade-on-delete requirement is only verified for the user_id foreign key; the entity_id cascade declared at database/migrations/2026_10_29_043320_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16 has no test, so deleting an entity would silently leave memberships behind if the constraint were wrong.

A global function memberOf() is declared at file scope in a Pest test; because all test files share one PHP process, it can collide with another file defining the same helper, so a dataset or closure would be safer.
The same isManager() logic is duplicated in app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:35; one shared helper (or a User method) would avoid the copy, though the duplication is small.

The doc says the 'at least one owner' half of the invariant is enforced 'by the application', but no code in this change enforces it (entity creation is out of scope), so the statement is currently aspirational.

review.summary: This change adds the entities/entity_memberships persistence layer, the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole models, factories, User relations and both policies, with broad Pest coverage and updated schema docs/changelog. It fully meets the requirements and contract, and the stored generated owner_seq column plus named unique indexes is the correct portable way to enforce one owner per entity. The only substantive gap is an untested entity-delete cascade, alongside a few minor nits, so it is approvable with small fixes.
